text:
alex: Heads-up — I sketched a lightweight load-harness proposal for kernel selection + KV cache behavior testing. Goal: get reproducible deltas for quant profiles and speculative decoding before we open a regression gate.

mira: drop it pls. TL;DR?

alex: short: hybrid traces (replay + synthetic shots) -> deterministic batching windows -> per-kernel microbench run -> end-to-end load with KV warmup policy toggles. Compare p50/p95, token-cost, and quality on golden prompt set.

david: love it. how do you intend to isolate kernel perf vs scheduling noise?

alex: microbench isolates kernel latency by running sequences with fixed batch/length and pinned cache state. then we run full harness to capture scheduling + queuing. Noise model: repeated seeds + jackknife CI.

oliver: can we make the harness non-invasive for CI? i.e., short smoke that fails fast if p95 regressed > X ms, longer nightly for full stats.

alex: yes — two tiers. smoke: 5 mins, canonical traces, KV warmup disabled, target = detect >10% p95 regression. overnight: 2 hours, full warmup, autoscaler engaged.

sophia: want to call out quantization experiments — some profiles change token distribution; need to measure oracle-quality delta (emd on token probs?) and not just perplexity.

david: +1. propose: golden prompt set (200 prompts) with human-rated threshold and automated rubric (exact-match, semantic-similarity).

perf-bot: [perf-regression-check] baseline run loaded: run_id=2026-03-18T11:04Z, p50=12.4ms, p95=48.9ms, mean_GPU_util=72%

alex: for kernel selection tests we should instrument kernel-name + kernel-launch-time in the trace. small example output:```
KERNEL=attn_fwd, seq=128, batch=8, time_us=1830
KERNEL=matmul_4bit, seq=256, batch=4, time_us=2340
```

mira: can we also tag whether call used KV cache hit vs miss? that affects matmul path.

alex: yes — tag frames with kv_state: cold/warm/hit. warm = cached keys but different prefix length.

oliver: how do we simulate real traffic? purely replay traces maybe biased.

alex: hybrid approach: replay for top 80% traffic shapes (from prod hist), and synthetic perturbations for tails (variable seq lengths, bursty arrival patterns). we also add adversarially long prefixes to stress KV.

sophia: speculative decoding experiments: measure wasted compute due to wrong top-k guesses. logging: speculative_attempts, rollback_count, wasted_tokens.

alex: exact logging example:```
speculative_attempts=1200, successful=1080, rollback=120, wasted_tokens=840
```

david: can we compute cost-per-successful-token and display alongside p95? that's helpful for cost-vs-quality tradeoffs.

alex: planned metric: tokens_processed_on_gpu, effective_output_tokens, cost_ratio = tokens_processed_on_gpu / effective_output_tokens.

mira: regression gate thresholds? ops wants a single knob.

alex: proposal: three dims: perf delta (p95), quality delta (golden-set pass rate), cost delta (cost_ratio). gate blocks if perf>+15% OR quality<-2% OR cost>+20%. ops can relax for canaries.

oliver: make sure we surface which kernel caused regression — otherwise it's just a number.

alex: agreed. adding root-cause heuristics: attribute p95 delta to top-3 kernels by delta_time * invocation_count.

perf-bot: [smoke-run] 2026-03-18T12:00Z: smoke completed: p95 delta +3.2% vs baseline, quality delta -0.1%, cost_ratio +1.8% — no gate triggered.

sophia: sounds reasonable. next step: implement microbench harness and add kernel tagging. i'll own quant experiments.

david: i can wire the perf-bot to compute cost_ratio and attach top-3 kernel attribution.

mira: schedule pairing session to review harness output format. 30m tomorrow?

alex: booked 10:30am PT. attaching planned output schema in thread in case folks want to pre-read:```
- run_id (string)
- workload_shape (replay|hybrid|synthetic)
- kv_policy (cold|warm|hit)
- batch_config (B,S)
- metrics: p50_ms, p95_ms, gpu_tokens, effective_tokens, cost_ratio, quality_pass_rate
- kernel_attribution: list of (kernel_name, delta_ms, invocations)
- speculative_stats: attempts, success, rollbacks, wasted_tokens
```

oliver: quick nit — kernel_attribution as list OK but make it compact CSV in logs so perf-bot can parse easily.

alex: noted. I'll PR the harness readme after microbench code lands. thanks all :thumbsup:
